young_sea_level.note: The crust takes the seas' water at a 17 cm a year fall if delivery stopped; the sag lowers the deep floors 1.5 cm a year under the central mantle and up to 41 cm a year under the warm profile in the first millennium (geography README). Where delivery lags, the young deltas build into a moving sea.

evidence: A screen: closed-form relations evaluated per mouth on 1-D arrays, no morphodynamic model. Mouths, rock and delta areas are the terrain study's routing on geography's drainage (16 px/deg, older climate run A28_dim5_moon); flows are bracketed for the design climate; temperatures are design estimates from the design years' land air by aridity class; soils are candidates, not choices; waves come from the wave study where it computed them and from fetch-limited growth elsewhere.
reading_rule: States: young (regolith, bare banks, own-catchment rock times the young yield factor, drier rivers, soft young seas) and mature (each candidate soil, rooted banks, the terrain study's cases, held seas). Shares of mouths are by count, of discharge by mean flow, of load by rock. Plume shares are of the ten tenths of the lunar day, at mean flow and at bankfull. Dominance follows Nienhuis et al. (2020): the largest of the river's, the waves' and the tide's sediment flux. Lengths in m unless named in km, times in years, discharges m3/s, loads kg/s or Mt a year as named.
